puzzles.title: The broad-market fall
puzzles.scenario: The Nifty falls 12% in one month. Your diversified holdings remain profitable and their forecasts are unchanged.
puzzles.question: Which response best protects a sound long-term process?
choices: Sell everything because the portfolio fell
Review fundamentals and rebalance only where the evidence changed
Move the entire portfolio into the previous month's winner
puzzles.explanation: A market fall is an outcome, not proof that every underlying decision became weak. Recheck the evidence before changing the portfolio.

puzzles.title: Growth at any price?
puzzles.scenario: Company A has strong expected growth but a PEG of 3.2. Company B has slightly lower growth, comparable quality and a PEG of 1.1.
puzzles.question: Which fact most strongly supports considering Company B?
choices: Its share price is lower
Its growth appears available at a more reasonable valuation
It must rise next month
puzzles.explanation: PEG relates the price paid to expected growth. It does not guarantee returns, but it helps distinguish attractive growth from expensive expectations.

puzzles.title: One winner becomes the portfolio
puzzles.scenario: A successful holding has grown to 46% of your portfolio while several strong opportunities remain available.
puzzles.question: What is the main portfolio risk?
choices: The portfolio owns too many sectors
One company's setback can dominate the entire result
The holding's past gain will automatically reverse
puzzles.explanation: A strong company can still create a weak portfolio when its weight makes one outcome disproportionately important.

puzzles.title: Smooth versus spectacular
puzzles.scenario: Portfolio A returned 18% with 12% volatility. Portfolio B returned 21% with 29% volatility. Their other evidence is similar.
puzzles.question: Which portfolio has the clearer risk-adjusted case?
choices: Portfolio A
Portfolio B
They are identical because both made money
puzzles.explanation: The extra return in Portfolio B came with much more instability. Sharpe-style reasoning rewards return earned efficiently, not return alone.

puzzles.title: The hidden cost of recovery
puzzles.scenario: Two portfolios have similar annual returns. Portfolio A's worst peak-to-trough fall is 14%; Portfolio B's is 39%.
puzzles.question: Why does Portfolio A deserve serious consideration?
choices: It is guaranteed to outperform
It required a shallower loss and less recovery to regain its peak
Drawdown matters only to traders
puzzles.explanation: Large losses require disproportionately larger gains to recover. Drawdown measures the difficult journey hidden by an end return.

puzzles.title: Cheap for a reason
puzzles.scenario: A stock's PE has fallen sharply, but its profit forecast, balance-sheet quality and risk-adjusted return have all deteriorated.
puzzles.question: What is the strongest interpretation?
choices: A lower PE always makes it a bargain
The stock may be a value trap and needs evidence of business resilience
Buy because the market is wrong
puzzles.explanation: A low valuation is useful only when the earnings and business supporting it remain credible.

puzzles.title: Twelve names, one bet
puzzles.scenario: Your portfolio owns twelve stocks, but nine depend heavily on the same commodity cycle.
puzzles.question: Is this portfolio well diversified?
choices: Yes, because it has twelve tickers
No, because common economic exposure can make the holdings fall together
Yes, if every holding has a low PE
puzzles.explanation: Ticker count is not enough. Useful diversification comes from exposures that do not all respond to the same risk.

puzzles.title: Good company, smaller role
puzzles.scenario: A holding remains healthy, but its weight and valuation have risen while other holdings now offer better risk-adjusted upside.
puzzles.question: Which move best reflects disciplined rebalancing?
choices: Hold forever because the company is healthy
Trim the position without treating it as a failed investment
Sell every profitable holding
puzzles.explanation: A trim changes the role of a sound holding when the portfolio can use capital more efficiently elsewhere.

puzzles.title: A normal bad month
puzzles.scenario: A one-month 95% VaR estimate is ₹18,000 for a ₹5 lakh portfolio.
puzzles.question: What does this estimate most nearly mean?
choices: The portfolio cannot lose more than ₹18,000
In the model, about 5% of months may be worse than a ₹18,000 loss
The portfolio will lose exactly ₹18,000 next month
puzzles.explanation: VaR is a model threshold, not a maximum-loss guarantee. Tail losses beyond it remain possible.

puzzles.title: The expensive share
puzzles.scenario: Your best theoretical allocation requires half a share of a ₹8,000 stock, but BTI permits whole shares only and your monthly contribution is ₹10,000.
puzzles.question: What should the evaluator compare you against?
choices: An impossible fractional portfolio
The best feasible whole-share portfolio for your actual cash and holdings
The ₹1 lakh campaign's portfolio
puzzles.explanation: A fair benchmark respects the player's actual constraints. Skill is measured against the best feasible opportunity, not an unattainable answer.

puzzles.title: Different weights, equally strong
puzzles.scenario: Your portfolio differs from the hidden reference weights but has nearly identical expected return, downside risk, valuation quality and diversification.
puzzles.question: How should BTI classify it?
choices: Blunder, because weights differ
Within the excellent-equivalence band
Best only if next month rises
puzzles.explanation: Portfolio problems can have several near-optimal solutions. BTI scores opportunity loss, not obedience to one exact weight vector.

puzzles.title: A forecast is not a fact
puzzles.scenario: A stock has the highest forecast return but also the widest uncertainty range and a severe historical drawdown.
puzzles.question: What is the disciplined response?
choices: Allocate everything to the highest forecast
Size it only after considering uncertainty and portfolio downside
Ignore all forecasts permanently
puzzles.explanation: A forecast is one input. Position size should reflect both its potential and how uncertain or damaging the downside could be.
